f1.quote: The study compressed the [1̄23]-oriented single crystals and determined the CRSS for (111)[1̄01] slip across temperature

f2.quote: CRSS–temperature data outside the inertial and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes were fitted with a conventional thermal-activation equation to extrapolate CRSS to 0 K

f3.quote: Compression was conducted from 9 to 1373 K at an engineering strain rate of 1 × 10^-4 s^-1

f4.quote: Composition-dependent local lattice distortion/MSAD and the resulting dislocation glide-resistance landscape mediate solid-solution strength

f5.quote: At cryogenic temperatures, a reduced phonon drag coefficient permits dislocation inertial motion

f6.quote: The PL behavior is most consistent with Cottrell-type elastic solute–dislocation attraction, particularly involving Mn and Fe

f7.quote: No measurable widening of dissociated partials or reduction of stacking-fault energy was observed after high-temperature deformation of CrFeNi

f8.quote: Relative to room-temperature deformation, cooling was expected to substantially raise CRSS

f10.quote: the increase becoming less steep below about 77 K because of dislocation inertia

f11.quote: heating into the diffusion-active regime was expected to cause a small CRSS increase and serrated flow through the PL effect
